supersedes.reason: The pre-fix run resolved its derived-edge reader by the record's Graphiti group_id (finding.project_id) against a reader dict keyed by the --project GRAPH NAMES. Any episode whose group_id differed from the graph it was read from therefore resolved to the wrong reader, or to no reader at all, and the miss serialized as `derived_edge_uuids: []` — indistinguishable from a measured zero. Fixed in steps 16-19 (commits b3b1ff99fb, dcfedcccd6, 041b6277f1, 994e6667f4): the lookup is now keyed on the new `graph_name` field (WHICH GRAPH WAS QUERIED), and a genuinely un-enumerated edge list serializes as JSON `null` with `edges_unqueried: true` rather than as an empty list.

notes: report.json is byte-for-byte the script's stdout. It was neither pretty-printed nor hand-edited. All logging went to stderr.

THIS RUN SUPERSEDES THE 2026-08-12 ONE — see `supersedes` above for the defect and the fixing commits. The stale artifact was NOT left in place and was NOT hand-patched to look fixed; the whole sweep was re-run against the live store.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY CHANGED, MEASURED. Comparing the two reports finding-by-finding on (record_uuid, claim_kind, subject, ref): 195 findings are common to both, 5 of which changed their derived_edge_uuids. All 5 went from a NON-EMPTY list (6-11 edges each) to an EMPTY one; NONE went the other way. The plan's expectation was that the pre-fix report 'understates the graph' — that is not what the measurement shows. The pre-fix error ran in BOTH directions: it left 15 findings un-enumerated (reported as [] having never been queried) AND it attributed another graph's edges to 5 findings.

WHY THOSE 5 LOST THEIR EDGES — and the cross-graph fact it exposes. All 5 are episodes READ FROM the reify graph whose own group_id is 'dark_factory'. The pre-fix lookup keyed on group_id, so it queried the DARK_FACTORY graph and found edges there. Measured directly over GRAPH.RO_QUERY on 2026-08-15 for 3 of the 5: episode a887c958-0018-4715-8817-cf048c187e8d exists as an Episodic node ONLY in reify (count 1 in reify, 0 in dark_factory) yet has 8 RELATES_TO edges ONLY in dark_factory (8 in dark_factory, 0 in reify); 52a37f90-1f21-462f-96f6-9bf1774f3c32 -> node reify only, 11 edges dark_factory only; 0c5b3f7b-38e1-4436-baa6-4d8419f88645 -> node reify only, 7 edges dark_factory only. So an episode's derived edges CAN live in a different graph from the episode node. The corrected sweep enumerates edges only in the graph the episode was read from, which is the correct and predictable rule, but it means an empty list means 'none in THIS graph', not 'none anywhere'. That bound is now shipped as a first-class CAVEATS entry naming this exact episode, and cross-graph enumeration is filed as follow-up work rather than built here (it is beyond this task's plan).

THE 15 PREVIOUSLY-UNQUERIED FINDINGS ARE NOW GENUINELY QUERIED. Every finding whose project_id is not a swept graph name (know_live 10, knowlive 4, solar_challenge_platform 1) still shows []. The VALUE is unchanged but its epistemic status is not: before the fix those were never asked, now they were asked and the answer is a measured zero. summary.edges_unqueried is 0 for this run and the sweep emitted no 'NOT enumerated' warning, which is the machine-checkable statement that nothing went un-enumerated.

21 findings in this report have graph_name != project_id (reify<-dark_factory 6, reify<-know_live 7, reify<-knowlive 4, dark_factory<-know_live 3, reify<-solar_challenge_platform 1). Both fields are reported on every finding precisely so this population is visible instead of being silently collapsed into one column.

THE DENOMINATOR IS A MOVING TARGET. The corpus grew from 7577 to 7595 Episodic nodes over the ~3 days between the two runs (dark_factory 3030->3042, reify 4547->4553). The store is live and being written throughout; 7595 is a snapshot at run time, not a fixed population. The finding delta below is partly this drift and partly the fix.

FINDING DELTA vs the 2026-08-12 run: 1 dropped, 2 added, 195 common. DROPPED: episode e64dbe6f-5df7-43a3-be1f-398ce55278cf / task 3584, which the earlier run observed 'pending'. dark_factory task 3584 is now 'cancelled' (read from tasks.db on 2026-08-15), and 'cancelled' is in shared.task_statuses.TERMINAL, so the claim now VERIFIES and the finding disappeared. That is CAVEAT 2 firing live and measured: work that was cancelled — i.e. never landed — reads as verified. Both are Class A false positives (a filing claim about a task that exists but is not terminal); neither is a fabrication.

esc-3085-1 INSTANCE (2) WAS SWEPT AND CAME BACK CLEAN, unchanged from the earlier run. The 167 'mismatch' findings in report.json are the SCRIPT'S RAW VERDICTS, not adjudicated fabrications. The three systematic false-positive classes identified in investigation.md account for all 167 (Class A 127, Class B 10, Class C 30), and the conclusion is unchanged from the earlier run: 0 confirmed new fabrications of the esc-3085-1 shape. report.json is committed unedited precisely so that adjudication can be re-checked against the raw output.

Cross-repo commit verification (investigation.md class C) was performed OUT OF BAND for the earlier run with `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` run directly in /home/leo/src/dark-factory and /home/leo/src/reify at 2026-08-12T13:1xZ. The commit-subject population is byte-identical between the two runs (35 findings, 30 mismatch), so that adjudication carries over unchanged and was NOT re-derived. The script itself never performs that cross-repo check; it probes only the claimed project.

INVARIANT HELD: this sweep invalidated nothing and deleted nothing. Every episode and edge the report names is left exactly as it was, for human adjudication. The script has no --apply/--invalidate/--delete path, an absence pinned by TestReadOnlyByConstruction, and reads exclusively over GRAPH.RO_QUERY. The three ad-hoc verification queries quoted in these notes were likewise issued as GRAPH.RO_QUERY, and the tasks.db reads used sqlite mode=ro.
